podcast.body: Following the success of "I Got a Woman," Charles continued to rework gospel songs into rock and roll classics, taking the old gospel song "This Little Light of Mine" and transforming it into "This Little Girl of Mine." This demonstrated his formula of fusing sacred and secular music. "As next single, he took the old gospel song, This Little Light of Man. And reworked it into This Little Girl of Man."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 32: "I Got A Woman" by Ray Charles

podcast.body: Ray Charles famously and blatantly transformed the gospel song "This Little Light of Mine" into the secular "This Little Girl of Mine," exemplifying the mid-1950s trend of adapting gospel material by changing a few words, often "Jesus" to "baby" or similar. "Most famously and blatantly there was very Charles who did things like take this little light of mind. I'm turning it into this little girl of mine."
